articles.title_en: The faces behind the feeds: Gen Z’s private lives and public posts – in pictures
articles.title_ru: The faces behind the feeds: Gen Z’s private lives and public posts – in pictures
articles.preview_en: For the first digital natives, there are two places to express yourself: in the comfort of your own room and online.
articles.preview_ru: For the first digital natives, there are two places to express yourself: in the comfort of your own room and online.
articles.full_en: For the first digital natives, there are two places to express yourself: in the comfort of your own room and online. Photographer Niccolò Rastrelli set out to find out how the identities compare Social media arrived just as I, a younger millennial, was on the brink of teenhood. My friends and I signed up for accounts on Facebook, Myspace and Twitter, as well as less remembered sites such as the now defunct Bebo. We didn’t know what we were doing; no one did. We posted indiscreet messages and photos on public feeds that we wouldn’t want any future employer – or really anyone, for that matter – to see. Then gradually we, and our parents and their parents, too, learned what it means to live with that world-changing phenomenon that we term social media. We started to find different ways to adapt, a process that is ongoing.
